overview.geometryNote: Zome on a 10-sided plan. Six horizontal bands of rhombic panels labelled z1 (apex) through z5, plus a base course of triangular half panels and a set of mirrored special panels around the doorway. Unlike the 16' and 20' zomes this one carries past the widest point, so the walls tuck back in at the base - hence the acorn silhouette and the two short 'special base sections' either side of the door. All struts are the same length; only the miter and bevel angles change from band to band.
overview.bandNote: The plan names only five panel shapes but draws six rings of rhombi. The sixth (lowest) ring must reuse one of the five shapes. Its top bevel has to be 14.2 to meet z5's bottom bevel of 14.2, which points at z4 turned upside down - yet the component list gives the doubled quantity to z3 (17) and only 9 to z4. See pdfIssues; verify against the SketchUp model before cutting.

strut.countNote: 251 is printed on the Exploded View sheet, but the identical figure is printed on Trillium's 16' and 20' zome plans too, which have different panel counts. Treat it as boilerplate and count off the panel schedule instead.

length.note: Identical for every regular panel edge and for every special-panel edge that lies on the zome surface. Printed as 2'-0 1/4" on the Regular Panel sheet and as 2'-1/4" on the special panel sheets - same number.

crossSection.note: The plans publish no strut cross-section. Materials call for (16) 2x6x8' / 38x140x2.44 kiln-dried for the frame, and the builders method has you rip the strut stock in half on the table saw at the bevel angle. Finished section is builder-chosen; the jig is set to suit.

strut.bevelNote: There is no single bevel. Each band has a top bevel (the two struts pointing toward the apex) and a bottom bevel (the two pointing down/out). Where two bands meet the bevels match, so the numbers chain: 11.1 / 6.3 / 8 / 11.1 / 14.2 / 14.2. See panels[].bevels.
strut.miterNote: Every miter angle in these plans is stated OFF 90 degrees - the number is what you dial into the miter saw. Within one rhombus panel all four struts share the same miter.

pdfIssues.sheet: Regular Panel Dimensions (sheet 4) and Special Panels (sheet 6), both units
pdfIssues.issue: The z5 miter is printed as 15 deg. It disagrees with the plan's own dimensions. The printed z5 mid length (3'-2 11/16" / 983 mm) against the 2'-0 1/4" / 615 mm strut gives a corner angle of about 106 deg, so the saw setting should be about 16.0 deg (15.9 deg from the metric numbers). The z5 half drawing on sheet 6 makes the same error: its other two corners are printed 37 and 37, which forces the third to be 16.0, not 15. For comparison, Trillium's 16' zome uses the identical angle set and prints 15.7 deg for this corner on its own special panel sheet.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - a 1 deg miter error accumulates around a ten-panel band

pdfIssues.sheet: Special Panels (sheet 5) - z2 half, both units
pdfIssues.issue: The two base miters are printed 29.5 deg. With a 2'-0 1/4" / 615 mm side and a 1'-10 3/4" / 578 mm base, the base corners are 62.0 deg, so the saw setting should be about 28.0 deg. As printed the three miters imply interior angles summing to 176.9 deg, which cannot be a triangle. 29.5 deg is the correct value for the same panel on Trillium's 20' zome plan, so this looks like a copy-paste.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - the panel will not close on the frame

pdfIssues.sheet: Special Panels (sheet 6) - z3 quarter, both units
pdfIssues.issue: The miter at the corner between the 2'-0 1/4" / 615 mm strut edge and the 11 15/16" / 304 mm bottom edge is printed 34.8 deg. The three printed side lengths (615, 479, 304 mm) give 49.8 deg at that corner, i.e. a saw setting of about 40.2 deg. The other two printed miters (61 and 11.3) both match the lengths, so 34.8 is the odd one out; no combination of the three printed miters sums to 180 deg.
Stated '13 special panels' but the itemised list adds to 15 (z2 half 1 + z3 half vertical 2 + z3 half base 8 + z3 quarter 2 + z5 half 2). The regular-panel total of 53 does check out.

pdfIssues.sheet: Exploded View (sheet 3) vs Regular Panel Dimensions (sheet 4), both units
pdfIssues.issue: Which rhombus the sixth (lowest) band uses is ambiguous. The exploded plan view draws six rings of rhombi, and the component list gives z3 a doubled quantity (17) with z4 only 9, implying the sixth ring is z3. But the bevel table requires the band below z5 to present a 14.2 deg top bevel to match z5's 14.2 deg bottom bevel, and only z4 turned upside down does that - z3's bevels are 8 and 11.1. On that reading z4 should be the doubled type (about 17) and z3 the single band (about 9). Both readings give the same 53 total, and the z3 and z4 rhombi have nearly identical areas, so the material take-off is unaffected either way - but the cut counts per shape are not. Check against the supplied SketchUp model before cutting.
pdfIssues.severity: high - could put you 8 panels short of one shape and 8 long of another

pdfIssues.issue: '251 struts' is printed here and also on Trillium's 16' and 20' zome plans, which have different panel counts. It cannot be right for all three.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - do not order stock off this number

pdfIssues.sheet: Base Sections - non-Beveled Method (sheet 9), METRIC edition
pdfIssues.issue: The bottom plate thickness is printed 9 mm. The imperial sheet gives 1 1/2" and the metric beveled sheet gives 38 mm. 9 mm is a typo for 38 mm.
pdfIssues.severity: moderate - metric-only builders would size the plate wrong

pdfIssues.issue: The triangle base is labelled 820 mm on the drawing but 819 mm in the cut list on the same sheet. The imperial edition says 2'-8 1/4" in both places.
The nesting diagram draws far fewer panels than the component list requires (8 z1, 3 z2, 11 z3, 9 z4, 8 z5, 4 z3.5 base against 53 regular plus 15 special). It is a partial layout, not a take-off.

The stated height of 9'-6" / 2896 mm does not reconcile with the geometry. Seven strut-rises of frame plus the beveled base sections and plate come to roughly 9'-1" / 2764 mm. The stated widest diameter of 10'-7" / 3226 mm is likewise about 45 mm more than the frame centreline geometry. Both cover figures look rounded up or measured over the finished roofing.

No strut cross-section is published anywhere. Builders have to infer it from the materials list (2x6 stock) plus the builders-method instruction to rip strut stock in half at the bevel angle. The method says other strut dimensions are fine as long as they are consistent and the bevel angle is accurate.

Typographic sloppiness throughout: the z3 mid length prints as 2'-7 5/16 with no inch mark (sheet 4); the strut is 2'-0 1/4" on sheet 4 but 2'-1/4" on the special panel sheets; the deck cut list prints 3-10 9/16" and the bench list 2-9 1/16" with no foot mark; the bench elevation prints 1-8 1/2"; the non-beveled base layout prints 3'-1 5/16 with no inch mark. Compressed forms like 2'-11/16" and 3'-13/16" mean 2'-0 11/16" and 3'-0 13/16".
